editorial:
Imagine landing in the middle of Nebraska in the 1880s, but instead of exciting gunfights and gold rushes, you find a lonely, gray town. You meet a Swedish immigrant who has read way too many cheap novels about the Wild West. He arrives at the Blue Hotel thinking he is in a grand adventure, but he is completely out of touch with reality. He starts seeing enemies everywhere and acts so strange that he makes everyone around him uncomfortable. It is a slow burn that shows how a simple misunderstanding can turn a whole group of people against one lonely guy.

You will really appreciate the acting here because the tension builds up in a way that feels very real. The pacing is a bit slow, but that is the point; it makes you feel the boredom and isolation of the hotel guests. If you enjoy stories about how people treat outsiders, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older TV movie, you might want to look for a remastered 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture. If you are in a rush, renting it on Apple TV is your best bet for a quick watch.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when the Swede's paranoia reaches a breaking point. He believes the other guests are plotting against him, which leads to a violent clash. In the end, he is killed, but the movie leaves you wondering who the real villain was. Was it the Swede for being unstable, or the hotel guests for mocking him and pushing him over the edge? It ends on a sad note about how hate grows.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and historical dramas.
